To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inflation in the Russian economy in the period 1998–2013 has been generated mainly by the deviation of the money supply from the money demand, rather then the money supply itself.
inflation in Russia is determined by a combination of factors and that monetary factor plays an important role in the inflationary dynamics of the Russian economy.
the relationship between monetary factor and inflation is complex and non-linear.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: the role of money supply in the formation of inflation in the Russian economy, the relationship between the volume of money in circulation and inflation, and the impact of money on inflation.
the problem of identifying the relationship between money and prices, and the results obtained are of great interest for the monetary authorities of Russia.

the following issues: (i) what is the relationship between money supply and inflation in Russia; (ii) how to identify and model this relationship in order to make it more reliable; (iii) what is the role of money supply as an inflationary factor in Russia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Russian economy has experienced a transition from the stage of inflationary pressures caused by monetary factors to a stage where the main sources of inflationary pressure are the demand and supply factors.
the monetary factor is one of the key determinants of inflation in the Russian economy.
in the Russian economy the role of monetary factor as an inflation generator has increased in comparison with the 1990s, but it is still not as high as in the developed market economies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

monetary factor has an important role in the formation of the inflationary pressures and the inflationary dynamics in the Russian economy, and this impact should be taken into account in the anti-inflationary policy.
the relationship between money supply and inflation in Russia has been changing over time, and the monetary factor has become less important for the generation of inflation.
the Russian economy is not characterized by a stable long-run relationship between money and prices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the monetary factor is an important component of the inflation dynamics.

the relationship between money and prices is a complex and multidirectional process that requires a more comprehensive approach to the analysis of the inflationary process in Russia, which should take into account the role of monetary factor, as well as the impact of demand and supply factors on inflation.
the monetary factor is an important source of inflation in the Russian economy, which should be taken into account in the monetary policy.
